lines.text: Imagine cutting your own tent open, and running into the snow in your socks.
lines.beat_before: hook: inside the tent, a blade through the canvas, frame 0

lines.text: February, nineteen fifty nine. Nine experienced hikers camp on a slope in the northern Urals.
lines.beat_before: the slope at dusk, nine torches, the tent

lines.text: Weeks later, searchers find the tent. Cut open, from the inside.
lines.beat_before: the tent half buried, slashed canvas

lines.text: Footprints lead down the slope. Socks. Bare feet.
lines.beat_before: prints going downhill, toward the trees

lines.text: Some are found by a small fire, under a cedar tree.
lines.beat_before: the cedar, the dead fire, branches broken high up

lines.text: Others lie in a ravine. They are not found until May.
The file closes with three words: a compelling natural force.
In twenty twenty one, scientists showed how a delayed slab avalanche could explain the tent.
lines.beat_before: a slab breaks above the tent
the tent alone in the wind

lines.text: Whatever happened that night, nine people decided the frozen dark was safer than their tent.
